comments.text: One thing I don't understand about the simulations training AI such as locomotion; why don't they incorporate some kind of stamina or muscle fatigue? Even variable such as friction against the ground would be helpful to throw some rails on the learning process. No living being would move if it causes even slight damage to them, nor any designer design a robot that grinds itself down prematurely. But give them incentive to move to energy sources with minimal energy loss and minimal damage, we'd get a more realistic journey of typical evolution of mammals at least.

comments.author: @RasmusSchultz
comments.text:
Regarding GPTs: I find they are mostly a disappointment. What was promised is that these would be "experts" in different topics - what they delivered is a custom system prompt with optional RAG search. That's not groundbreaking at all - it's just a convenience for something we've already had for a long time in apps that use the API.

And it does not work well. For example, a TypeScript GPT does not know the latest TypeScript syntax, and a Docker GPT gives advice using older Docker syntax, and so on - you can't fix that with just RAG, improving these problems would require fine-tuning of the model on updated documentation, which is what I thought we were getting, but no.

The way they've published GPTs is not transparent either, at all. You would want to at least know if a GPT is just a system prompt (low effort) or a carefully organized collection of documents. I strongly suspect a lot of GPTs do not even have a substantial set of documents to refer to.

But even then, RAG just doesn't make a model "better" at anything - it's more comparable to someone pretending to be an expert, but really, they're secretly looking up every answer in an encyclopedia, without a real thorough understanding of the answer they give.

It's weird and a little surprising as well, because they have the APIs that allow fine-tuning - so they could implement this feature. I'm guessing they won't, because fine-tuning (and storing and loading mass amounts of fine-tuned models) is obviously a lot more expensive.

GPTs are a cheap and disappointing feature - there is nothing new about it, it lacks transparency, and that's why it hasn't made a "splash".
